extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in geometric analysis / Ricci flow
extracted.subtask_short: Ricci flow monotonicity and max principles
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, definitions and sufficient conditions used to prove monotonicity of Perelman functionals (F, λ, W, µ, ν) and to apply maximum principles for scalar and tensor quantities under the Ricci (and Kähler-Ricci) flow. Includes first-variation formulas, coupled evolution systems, monotonicity identities, and hypotheses ensuring preservation of positivity and convex sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Breather
rubrics_metrics.description: A metric g_{ij}(t) evolving by the Ricci flow is called a breather if for some t1 < t2 and α > 0 the metrics α g_{ij}(t1) and g_{ij}(t2) differ only by a diffeomorphism; α = 1, α < 1, α > 1 correspond to steady, shrinking and expanding breathers, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ricci solitons are trivial breathers (metrics differ by diffeomorphism+scaling for every pair t1,t2). This definition is used to characterize periodic/recurring solutions modulo diffeomorphism and scaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's F-functional — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: F(g_{ij}, f) = ∫_M (R + |∇f|^2) e^{-f} dV, defined for a Riemannian metric g_{ij} and smooth function f with R the scalar curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F is defined on the space of metrics and smooth functions; plays the role of an energy whose variation relates to the Ricci flow viewed as a gradient-type flow (see next items).

rubrics_metrics.name: First variation formula for F
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 1.5.2: For variations δg_{ij} = v_{ij} and δf = h, with v = g^{ij}v_{ij}, the first variation is given by an integral expression (in particular terms involving v_{ij}(R_{ij}+∇_i∇_j f) and (v/2 - h)(2Δf - |∇f|^2 + R)) against e^{-f} dV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit first-variation is the foundational identity used to derive monotonicity formulae for F under suitably coupled evolutions of g and f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coupled flow for (g,f) used with F and monotonicity identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the coupled system with the metric evolving by Ricci flow (∂_t g_{ij} = -2 R_{ij}) and f evolving by a backward heat-type equation (∂_t f = -Δ f + |∇f|^2 - R + ... as given in the text). Under this coupled flow d/dt F(g(t),f(t)) = 2 ∫ |R_{ij} + ∇_i∇_j f|^2 e^{-f} dV ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hence F is nondecreasing in time; monotonicity is strict unless the solution is a steady gradient soliton. Also (∫_M e^{-f} dV) is constant along this coupled evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — λ-functional
rubrics_metrics.description: λ(g_{ij}) = inf_{f, ∫ e^{-f} dV = 1} F(g_{ij},f). Equivalently, via u = e^{-f/2}, λ equals the first eigenvalue of the operator -4 Δ + R with the L^2 normalization ∫ u^2 dV = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: λ is invariant under diffeomorphism. It is obtained by minimizing F under the mass constraint; minimizers satisfy an Euler–Lagrange equation. λ is used to detect soliton behavior and monotonicity properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity and rigidity for λ
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary 1.5.4: λ(g(t)) is nondecreasing along the Ricci flow; monotonicity is strict unless on a steady gradient soliton. Consequently, a steady breather must be a steady gradient soliton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the minimizer f0 at some time and run the backward heat equation to compare λ at earlier times; invariance under diffeomorphism ensures comparison on breathers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaled λ̄-functional and expanding case criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Define λ̄(g) = λ(g) V(g)^{2/n} where V is volume. Corollary 1.5.5: λ̄(g(t)) is nondecreasing along the Ricci flow whenever it is nonpositive; monotonicity is strict unless on a gradient expanding soliton. Thus an expanding breather must be an expanding gradient soliton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This scale-invariant modification handles expanding cases; choose scaling parameter appropriately when comparing times on a breather.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence — breathers on compact manifolds are Einstein
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 1.5.6: On a compact manifold, a steady or expanding breather is necessarily an Einstein metric (combining monotonicity results and prior propositions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from the previous monotonicity/ridigity statements and structure results about solitons on compact manifolds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's W-functional — definition and invariances
rubrics_metrics.description: W(g,f,τ) = ∫_M [ τ (R + |∇f|^2) + f - n ] (4 π τ)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV, with τ > 0. W is invariant under simultaneous scaling of τ and g (parabolic scaling) and invariant under diffeomorphisms: W(a φ^* g, φ^* f, a τ) = W(g,f,τ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: W is the appropriate functional for studying shrinkers; the normalization factor (4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{-f} and τ-dependence are crucial for scale invariance.

rubrics_metrics.name: First variation formula for W
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 1.5.7: For variations v_{ij} = δg_{ij}, h = δf, η = δτ, δW(v,h,η) equals an explicit integral involving τ v_{ij}(R_{ij}+∇_i∇_j f), (v/2 - h) times [τ( R + 2Δ f - |∇ f|^2) + f - n], and η times (R + |∇f|^2)/2 - n/(2τ), all integrated against (4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This variation underlies monotonicity identities for W under coupled evolution of (g,f,τ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coupled flow for (g,f,τ) and monotonicity for W
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 1.5.8: Under the system ∂_t g_{ij} = -2 R_{ij}, ∂_t f = -Δ f + |∇f|^2 - R + n/(2τ), ∂_t τ = -1, one has d/dt W(g(t),f(t),τ(t)) = 2 τ ∫ |R_{ij} + ∇_i∇_j f - (1/(2τ)) g_{ij}|^2 (4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV ≥ 0. Equality iff on a shrinking gradient soliton. Also (4πτ)^{-n/2} ∫ e^{-f} dV is constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central monotonicity identity for analyzing shrinkers; the choice ∂_t τ = -1 matches the parabolic backward time scaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — µ(g,τ) and ν(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: µ(g,τ) = inf_{f, (4πτ)^{-n/2} ∫ e^{-f} dV = 1} W(g,f,τ). ν(g) = inf_{τ>0} µ(g,τ). µ corresponds to the best constant in a logarithmic Sobolev inequality and minimizers solve a nonlinear Euler–Lagrange equation (τ(2Δ f - |∇ f|^2 + R) + f - n = µ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence, positivity and smoothness of minimizers are addressed (u = e^{-f/2} viewpoint). These quantities are used to detect shrinking solitons and analyze entropy-type monotonicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity and rigidity for µ (and ν)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary 1.5.9: µ(g(t), τ(t)) is nondecreasing along the Ricci flow (with appropriate τ(t)); monotonicity is strict unless on a shrinking gradient soliton. Hence shrinking breathers must be shrinking gradient solitons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue by taking a minimizer at a time and evolving backwards; uses invariance of W under scaling and diffeomorphism to compare breathers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a global barrier function with controlled derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 2.1.1: On a complete manifold with metrics g_{ij}(t) with uniformly bounded curvature for t ∈ [0,T], there exists a smooth function f on M with f(x) → ∞ as d_0(x,x_0) → ∞ and uniform bounds |∇ f|_{g(t)} ≤ C, |∇^2 f|_{g(t)} ≤ C for t ∈ [0,T].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an f is used as a weight/barrier function in maximum-principle arguments (e.g., add ε e^{At} f) to localize arguments on noncompact manifolds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum principle — preservation of nonnegativity of scalar curvature
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 2.1.2: If scalar curvature R of a Ricci flow solution g_{ij}(t) is nonnegative at t=0, then R ≥ 0 for all t ∈ [0,T].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the barrier f of Lemma 2.1.1 and the trick R + ε e^{At} f; choose A large so that the evolution inequality gives ∂_t (R + ε e^{At} f) > Δ (R + ε e^{At} f), then apply the maximum principle and let ε → 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton's tensor maximum principle (preservation of nonnegativity for bilinear forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 2.1.3: Let M_{αβ} be a symmetric bilinear form on a vector bundle V with metric h_{αβ}, evolving by ∂_t M_{αβ} = Δ M_{αβ} + u^i ∇_i M_{αβ} + N_{αβ}, where u^i(t) bounded and N_{αβ}=P(M_{αβ},h_{αβ}) is a polynomial in M. If initially M_{αβ} ≥ 0 and N_{αβ} satisfies the null-eigenvector condition N_{αβ} v^α v^β ≥ 0 whenever M_{αβ} v^α v^β = 0, then M_{αβ} ≥ 0 for all t ∈ [0,T].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof perturbs M by ε e^{At} f h_{αβ} where f is the barrier function; choose A large and apply scalar maximum-principle argument to the quadratic form M_{αβ} v^α v^β. This is the template for preserving positivity of curvature operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application — preservation of nonnegativity of curvature operator
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 2.1.4: Applying Lemma 2.1.3 to the curvature operator evolution ∂_t M = Δ M + M^2 + M^#, the nonnegativity of the curvature operator M_{αβ} is preserved by the Ricci flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The polynomial structure of the curvature operator evolution satisfies the null-eigenvector condition required by the tensor maximum principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kähler case — preservation of holomorphic bisectional curvature
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 2.1.5: Under the Kähler-Ricci flow, if the initial metric has positive (resp. nonnegative) holomorphic bisectional curvature then the evolved metric also has positive (resp. nonnegative) holomorphic bisectional curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: Bando (n=3), Mok (compact general n), Shi (noncompact). The same maximum-principle paradigm applies in the Kähler setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton's strong maximum principle for tensors — rank constancy and nullspace invariance
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 2.2.1: For M_{αβ} solving ∂_t M_{αβ} = Δ M_{αβ} + N_{αβ} on a bounded connected domain Ω with N_{αβ}=P(M_{αβ},h_{αβ}) and N_{αβ} ≥ 0 whenever M_{αβ} ≥ 0, if M_{αβ} ≥ 0 on Ω×[0,T] then there exists δ>0 such that on Ω×(0,δ) the rank of M_{αβ} is constant, and the nullspace of M_{αβ} is invariant under parallel translation and in time and lies in the nullspace of N_{αβ}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a carefully constructed test function ρ evolved by heat equation, and perturbations by ε e^{t} to force strict inequalities; shows rigidity information about nullspaces and yields structural consequences for curvature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence — image of curvature operator is Lie subalgebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 2.2.2: If the curvature operator M_{αβ} is nonnegative initially, then for some interval 0 < t < δ the image of M_{αβ} is a Lie subalgebra of so(n) with constant rank and invariant under parallel translation and in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from the strong maximum principle combined with the algebraic structure of the M^# term in the curvature evolution; relates curvature positivity to holonomy-type algebraic structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced maximum principle — invariance of closed convex bundles sets under PDE
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 2.3.1 (Hamilton): Let V be a vector bundle with time-dependent connection and Laplacian Δ_t. Let K be a closed subset of V such that (H1) K is invariant under parallel translation for each t, and (H2) each fiber intersection K_x is closed and convex. If for every x and any solution of the fiberwise ODE dσ_x/dt = N(x,σ_x,t) starting in K_x stays in K_x, then any uniformly bounded solution σ(x,t) of the PDE ∂_t σ = Δ_t σ + u^i ∇_i σ + N(x,σ,t) starting in K remains in K for later times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces PDE preservation questions to ODE invariance checks in each fiber. Boundedness of σ and the hypotheses (H1,H2) are required. Lemma 2.1.3 is a special case where K is the cone of nonnegative symmetric bilinear forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical lemmas used in advanced maximum principle — sup-derivative and Gronwall-type control
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 2.3.2: If ϕ(t) is Lipschitz and dϕ/dt ≤ C ϕ whenever ϕ≥0, then ϕ(t) ≤ 0 given ϕ(a) ≤ 0. Lemma 2.3.3: For ψ(x,t) smooth on compact Y, φ(t)=sup_{y∈Y} ψ(y,t) satisfies dφ/dt ≤ sup_{y with ψ=φ} ∂_t ψ(y,t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These analytic estimates bridge fiberwise ODE behavior and global PDE maxima; they are standard tools in the maximum principle arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: ODE characterization for invariance of closed convex sets (tangent cone condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 2.3.4: For an ODE dϕ/dt = N(ϕ,t) on an open U ⊂ R^n and closed convex Z ⊂ U, the ODE preserves Z (solutions starting in Z remain in Z) iff ϕ + N(ϕ,t) ∈ T_ϕ Z for all ϕ ∈ ∂Z and t, i.e., the vector field points into the tangent cone at boundary points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the precise algebraic/tangential criterion to check in each fiber when applying the advanced maximum principle: test N at boundary points against the tangent cone.
